title: Minimum absolute difference pairs → pairs at difference k
label: ag-multi
statement: Given an array of **distinct** integers, return every pair `(a, b)` with `a < b` whose difference `b − a` equals the **minimum absolute difference** between any two elements, in ascending order.
provenance: The top Agoda entry on CodeJeet (LeetCode 1200, 100%). A 2025 HackerRank OA report describes "pairs with minimum absolute difference equal to K" as its first question, a 2025 Taro report "minimum sum pairs — return all of them", and an onsite in Jun 2026 (FastPrep). Stage 2 follows the OA wording (LeetCode 532).

stages.title: All minimum-difference pairs
stages.say: Return every pair whose difference is the minimum difference in the array.
stages.require: Implement `MinAbsDiff.MinimumPairs(arr)`. Fewer than two elements → empty. Do not modify `arr`.

stages.title: Pairs at difference k
stages.say: The assessment version: count the unique pairs whose difference is exactly k. Values may repeat.
stages.require: Add `MinAbsDiff.CountPairsWithDiff(nums, k)`: unique value pairs with `y − x == k`, `k >= 0`.

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe after sorting, the minimum difference can only occur between neighbours, so one pass finds it and collects every neighbouring pair that matches; the k-difference count uses a frequency map so each unique pair is counted once. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Given an array of **distinct** integers, return every pair `(a, b)` with `a < b` whose difference `b − a` equals the **minimum absolute difference** between any two elements, in ascending order.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Are the values distinct? (Yes in stage 1; stage 2 allows duplicates.)
- May I reorder the input? (No — copy it.)
- Can differences overflow int? (Values span the full int range — use long.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: In sorted order the closest pair is always adjacent, so you never compare non-neighbours. Collect while you scan; when a smaller difference appears, clear the list.

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Sorting the caller's array in place.
- int overflow on s[i] - s[i-1] for extreme values.
- O(n²) all-pairs comparison.
- Counting (1,3) and (3,1), or duplicate values, more than once in the k version.
